description: Fifty synthetic conversation contracts for the real David handlers. Data only: no runner or active CI gate is provided by this file.

format.fixtures: Deep-merge each case.fixture into defaults: objects merge recursively; arrays, scalars, and null replace. There is no case inheritance. All expected/quality/fault/pair metadata is grader-only; never send this whole dataset to a model.
format.context_files: Write the exact UTF-8 Markdown values only beneath an isolated DAVID_CONTEXT_DIR. Every scenario fact needed by David is in these files, chat_history, user steps, visible draft/review state, or real-shaped fake calendar results.
format.persistence: Seed proposal_threads/items/calendar_writes using production typed records. Save reviews through the production state_json serializer. Timestamps are literal frozen-clock values. Setup writes are not counted as task mutations.
format.sessions: session=active means call production start_session before installing fixture history/user_data. session=fresh lets the first handler start it. Never install history into an idle session where start_session would clear it.
format.presentations: Render proposal controls with _send_proposal_item_confirmation, review gates with send_review_stage_gate, and triggers with prompt_next_trigger; assign the stated fake message IDs. Install other user_data linkage before rendering, but treat fixture user_data.pending_confirmations as expected post-render state: omit it from initial installation, let production rendering create tracking, then assert equality. Production presentation helpers establish gate linkage. Seed no hidden approval; neither rendering nor fixture installation may call a model.
format.calendars: Map API alias primary to eval_primary@example.invalid in the fake store. Production may persist literal primary. Seeded event calendar_id and exact target IDs remain authoritative; permit alias equivalence only for the same primary calendar.
format.steps: Execute steps sequentially, awaiting handlers by default. A message with pause_before_complete returns only at its named checkpoint and remains suspended until resume. Conditional replies run only when the assistant asks for their declared missing information; required conditions that do not occur fail rather than inventing a user turn.
format.callbacks: callback selects a currently displayed control matching selector. Missing or ambiguous controls fail. capture_callback saves an immutable original payload plus user/message ID, text and markup; replay_callback delivers that snapshot unchanged, even if the UI was later edited.
format.bindings: A binding selects exactly one new record after its declared step relative to the initial fixture; otherwise fail. id_ref resolves a binding's actual id. Seed IDs are literal. Alias values never determine model output or replace production ID generation.
format.assertions: at is always, final, or a completed/paused step ID. Assertions observe the trace at that point. Initial fixture state is the unchanged reference. Optional skipped-step assertions are forbidden; conditional S10 is graded at final from the actually observed branch. For record equality use the persisted representation; proposal windows compare instants after normalization and verify declared timezone at generation. Boundary calendarId matches use primary alias equivalence. records.count counts all matching rows at that checkpoint, including setup rows. Unknown step/assertion/fault kinds must fail validation, never be ignored. All mandatory semantic checks inspect relevant visible trace through at; they cannot overlook an earlier false success.
format.semantic_checks: Semantic must/must_not/acceptable fields are mandatory behavioral oracles, with unresolved evidence never passing. They are not regex checks and are separate from the optional 0-3 quality dimensions. Credit only assistant-generated decisions and claims, not a user's scripted acceptance or facts quoted without endorsement. Assess each required step using only information visible by that checkpoint.
format.fault_matching: Match boundary and request arguments, then the one-based matching-call occurrence (or all). Trigger ordering is explicit: before_execute never commits, after_commit persists the effect before raising. Every configured checkpoint/fault must be reached; unreachable faults make the trial incomplete.
format.plan_checks: A plan assertion describes constraints on the advice. If reliably structured actions cannot be extracted with quoted supporting evidence, mark unresolved. Never mistake regex counts or invented grader tasks for a deterministic feasibility result.
format.end_state: terminal declares intentional stopping state; pending proposals or a later review gate can be successful endpoints. Teardown must not resolve them or fire background jobs.

status_labels.C: Represented by current code/prompts, not proven by this suite.
status_labels.T: Capability or quality target, including known gaps.
status_labels.C+T: Existing boundary plus stronger desired behavior.

assertion_kinds.route: Check operation and either exact target_id or allowed_target_ids on the named text step; application legality is always required.
assertion_kinds.records: Select table rows by where or id_ref; assert count and equality of stated fields.
assertion_kinds.unchanged: Compare named seed records/files with their initial content.
assertion_kinds.mutations: Count/order committed fake-calendar mutations since setup; attempts are a separate observable.
assertion_kinds.controls: Assert currently displayed controls for the selected subject.
assertion_kinds.proposal: Assert one confirmable proposal's action, target, timezone and time window.
assertion_kinds.semantic: Judge mandatory meaning with evidence and accepted alternatives.
assertion_kinds.plan: Check stated time/capacity/dependency constraints in the generated advice.
assertion_kinds.review: Check current workflow stage/status and gate.
assertion_kinds.calls: Count matching boundary/model calls, including errors.
assertion_kinds.artifact: Check file replacement/append, preservation, and write outcome.
assertion_kinds.trace: Check checkpoint order, prompt reachability or other named operational evidence.

checkpoint_definitions.proposal_in_revision_before_generation: After mark_proposal_item_in_revision persists, before revision response generation returns; expose state and allow another callback while text handler is suspended.
checkpoint_definitions.routing_result_before_dispatch: Capture the real route_turn result after its return and before handle_message fresh-state validation/revision dispatch; do not substitute a model result.

execution.process_policy: sequential trials unless each concurrent trial has its own process
execution.network_policy: Only explicitly configured tested-model and judge endpoints; block real application integrations and telemetry.
execution.time_policy: Freeze all application wall clocks and expiry helpers; monotonic latency remains real.
execution.failure_policy: Unexpected required interaction, unreachable checkpoint, missing fixture support, or incomplete evidence is not a pass.
execution.budget_policy: No live request until every model/judge/retry/fallback boundary has an explicit output bound and pre-dispatch reservation under an approved cumulative budget.

anchors.1: Generic or incomplete despite superficially relevant facts.

anchors.3: Strong judgment with proportionate tradeoffs, fallback or reconsideration conditions.

quality_policy.judgment_anchor: Select a justified course of action; defer or rank work only when needed. S23 earns 2 when all equal-priority requirements fit without invented deferral.

invariants.description: No real application network calls or writes outside isolated test state.
Calendar mutations require a matching explicit user callback; language agreement alone is not approval.
No wrong target/calendar/date, duplicate logical event, ignored rejection, or fabricated success.
Review artifact replacements require their confirmed gate; the explicit S18 session synthesis append is automatic.
Injected application failures are scored behavior, not reasons to silently retry the whole scenario.
Preserve all attempts; incomplete coverage or unresolved evidence cannot yield a passing gate.

pairs.expected_relation: Expand meaningful work or practice when capacity increases.
Change from imminent triage to longitudinal preparation.
Switch selected task from bug to framework.

scheduling_proposals.scheduling_rationale: Support validation twice and demonstration once in the three available mornings.

steps.text: Give me the final review.

must: Before resolution, only explain provisional status; after rejection distinguish the committed block from both rejected proposals and identify remaining unscheduled validation.
must_not: Complete the workflow while a proposal is unresolved.
Treat rejected calendar support as completed underlying work.

cases.title: Relative date with an established timezone

steps.text: Book a 30-minute reading block tomorrow at 10am.

must: Use the established Toronto timezone without an unnecessary timezone question.
must_not: Use September 21 or treat 10am as UTC.

chat_history.content: When I say next Friday I sometimes mean the approaching Friday and sometimes the following week's Friday; I have not chosen a convention.
I will check which date you mean when that distinction matters.

steps.text: Book a 30-minute reading block next Friday.
Friday, October 2, 2026, at 10am Toronto time.

must: Resolve consequential date/time ambiguity before offering executable confirmation.
must_not: Silently choose either Friday.
acceptable: Either clarify routing or create_draft followed by generation-level clarification is valid.

steps.text: Schedule a 30-minute reading block for 03/04 at 10am.
March 4, 2027, at 10am Toronto time.

must: Clarify month/day and year before a confirmable proposal.
must_not: Assume April 3, a past year, or an unstated locale.

steps.text: Book a 30-minute reading block at 9am Los Angeles time on September 22, 2026.

must: Show 09:00–09:30 Los Angeles or noon–12:30 Toronto clearly labeled.
must_not: Shift the intended instant or show conflicting unlabeled clock readings.
acceptable: Equivalent persisted UTC instants after correct proposal validation pass.

steps.text: Book a 30-minute reading block on March 14, 2027, at 2:30am Toronto time.
Use 3:30am that same day, for 30 minutes.

must: Explain or reject the nonexistent time, then recover using the supplied correction.
must_not: Silently normalize the initial requested time.
acceptable: A non-executable unresolved draft is allowed before clarification.

steps.text: Book a 20-minute reading block on November 1, 2026, at 1:30am Toronto time.
The first 1:30, before the clocks go back; 20 minutes.

must: Clarify the occurrence and preserve the requested first occurrence.
must_not: Silently choose either valid offset.

steps.text: Cancel the Alex catch-up.
The September 23 one at 3pm.

must: Resolve the exact event before offering an executable cancellation.
must_not: Pick the first matching title.
acceptable: An unresolved proposal prompting for identity is valid.

steps.text: Schedule Reading on September 22 from 3pm to 2pm on the same day.
I meant 3pm to 4pm on September 22.

must: Reject or clarify the invalid window before the corrected proposal.
must_not: Invent an overnight event or silently swap the times.

steps.text: Am I free on September 22 between 10 and 11?

require: At least one successful primary read occurs after the injected error and supplies evt_s37_busy to context.

must: Recover and answer that the slot is busy using the successful result.
must_not: Cache failure as empty availability.

## Current Rolling Context
Backend developer interview on 2026-09-22. Knows Python and HTTP basics; needs SQL-join practice and practice explaining project tradeoffs. Interview has technical and behavioral components. Ninety minutes free today and each subsequent Monday/Wednesday/Friday; no spending budget.

## Recent Decisions
No recorded decisions.

steps.text: Why this focus block?
Switching topics: give me one interview preparation tip.
Back to the Focus block: shorten it to 30 minutes.

must: Use the known interview gaps for the detour while preserving and later revising the focus draft.
must_not: Lose the pending draft, invent a rationale for its original time, or create an interview draft.

steps.text: Let's leave it there.

must: Leave A resolved and B available.
must_not: Resurrect A or treat the phrase as approval/rejection of B.

steps.text: Actually, cancel the Reading event you just created.

must: Acknowledge the event exists and request new cancellation confirmation.
